result:
I played all 24 months. All three training runs were met and all inference demand was served, for a **net cost of $927.3M** with no penalties.

| | $M |
|---|---|
| GPU purchases | 532.5 |
| Cloud reservations | 384.4 |
| Power | 168.9 |
| Spot | 21.5 |
| Interest | 2.8 |
| Resale income | −21.2 |
| Value of GPUs still owned at the end | −221.7 |
| Contracts and power still owed after month 23 | +60.1 |

**What I did:**
- **Months 0–2:** I bought 21k gen-H GPUs: 18k from the vendor and 3k from broker A, which delivered. Together with the 14k already owned or on order, that made 35k. I also signed 30 MW of power early, because only 16 MW was available at the start.
- **Months 5 and 8:** I added 19 MW more power. The original 16 MW contract ended after month 19, and without the new power about a third of the GPUs would have sat idle.
- **Months 10–18:** The supply market stayed mostly loose and the cloud contract index fell from about $1.6M to $0.8M per kH-month. Inference demand grew about 7% a month, from 5.6 kH to 28 kH. To guard against a switch to tight supply, which could have meant a $200M+ missed-run penalty, I locked 20 kH of 12-month reservations at about $1.14M. I then added 6-month reservations at months 15 and 18, the second after gen N launched and cloud prices dropped.
- **Months 17–20:** I bought spot only in cheap months, at $0.65–0.85M per kH-month, to build a safety margin.
- **Month 23:** I sold 3k surplus H GPUs.

**Where money was wasted:**
- **Window 1:** I delivered 132 kH-months against 60 needed, because the early purchase came in faster than I'd planned for.
- **Window 2:** I delivered 257 against 140, mostly because the early 12-month reservations were insurance that ran through months 11–15. Supply never went tight, so in hindsight that insurance cost roughly $50–60M.
- **Power:** The 15 MW contract signed in month 8 only started in month 16, so most of its 24-month term was charged after the game ended. That accounts for much of the $60M still owed.

I recorded a belief-log note every month. Three of the early notes were partly cut off because I used semicolons, which the command line treats as separators, so a few phrases were rejected as unknown commands.
